title: Justice Department Files to Intervene and Dismiss Lawsuit that Would Hamper America’s AI Innovation and Security

reading.body:
The summary recorded for this incident is not a summary. It is a model's own message saying that the text it received was corrupted PDF code and that it could not produce the requested summary. The failure therefore sits in the document pipeline rather than in the model's reasoning, because raw PDF bytes reached the model instead of extracted text, and the model's reply was then stored as the incident's summary.

That places the failure on both sides of the model, at ingestion and at publication. Catching it would have taken a check that the extracted text was readable before it was sent, and a check that the returned output was actually a summary before it was published. Neither check is visible in the record. The incident is also titled after the Justice Department's filing, while the summary describes a failure to read a legal notice, so the catalogue entry and its own summary do not describe the same thing.

What the underlying reports establish is separate and narrower. The pollution claims, the Clean Air Act notice of intent to sue, the complaint by the NAACP and others, and the Justice Department's filing to intervene and dismiss are allegations and filings, not findings. Nothing here establishes that the plant violated the Clean Air Act, that any lawsuit will succeed, or that any party acted with intent.
